data.name: Kuber
data.long_meaning: In Hindu mythology, Kuber is the lord of wealth, prosperity, and trade. He is the king of Alaka Purusha, the Yaksha (nature spirit) king, and the god of the eastern direction. He is also known as the god of the mountains and the god of the crops. Kuber is said to possess a magical gem called the Mani Praptha Jyoti or the Cintamani, which is capable of fulfilling all desires.

in_sanskrit.name: कुबेर
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: कु- (to cup, to hold) + बेर- (to bear, to carry) = कु-बेर- (one who holds a cup, a cup-bearer)

in_hindi.name: कुबेर

in_telugu.name: కుబేర్

data.cultural_impact: Kuber holds a significant place in Hindu culture, especially in business communities where he is often invoked for wealth, success, and prosperity. His influence extends beyond money to include natural resources and agriculture. Many temples, especially in Nepal and India, are dedicated to Kuber, and he is often depicted with a gem, coins, or a pearl in various North Indian, Nepal Bihar, and Newari traditions.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, Kuber represents the divine aspect of wealth and its rightful usage. According to Hindu scriptures, material wealth is neither good nor bad. It depends on the consciousness and intentions of the individual. Thus, Kuber serves as a reminder that wealth and prosperity can be used spiritually to help others and enhance one's spiritual growth rather than just for personal gain. Additionally, Kuber, as a Yaksha king, represents the harmony between humans and nature, emphasizing the importance of preserving and respecting natural resources.
